findings.issue: The two order-case cards still stand in a narrow centred column (about 350–1090 px of the 1440 frame) under a heading, 'A recent order', that starts on the content's left edge, leaving about 330 px of empty tint on each side, so the cards float mid-page instead of following their heading (this was raised in the earlier review and the current shot still shows it).
findings.reference: The competitor's card sets start on the content's left edge under their heading and fill the content width (outlined cards in a row, 1px outline, about 28 px gutter).
findings.fix: In the template's patterns.css, stop centring `.order-cases` (max-width plus margin-inline: auto) when headings start: under `body[data-heading-align="start"]` set `.order-cases { margin-inline: 0; }`. Better still, set the cases side by side in a grid of equal columns from the left edge.

findings.issue: In the narrow left column of the two-column FAQ, 'Frequently Asked Questions' still breaks into three one-word lines, so the heading looks stacked rather than sized to its words (still unfixed in the current shot).
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ sets its heading across the width on one line, with the questions on hairline rows below it.
findings.fix: In the FAQ's two-column layout, widen the heading column. Or, when the template's fit would leave one word per line, set the heading above the questions.

findings.issue: The related-pages section has about twice the space above its heading (about 70 px against about 36 px in cases and overview) and under its link cards, which leaves a visible empty band between the tinted cases and FAQ sections; phones show the same extra space.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one even section gap down the page.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give `.block--related` the same padding-block as the other plain sections (remove whatever extra top/bottom padding or margin applies to `.block--related` or its heading).

findings.issue: The question 'Have you worked with small start-up brands placing their first order, like us?' breaks at the compound's hyphen, so the first line ends on 'start-' and the next begins with 'up brands'.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ questions keep each word whole on its line.
findings.fix: In Site Factory, write 'start-up' with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011), or reword it as 'small new brands'.

findings.issue: The open first answer is still one unbroken paragraph of about 370 words. That is about 40 lines on a phone and a dense block in the desktop column too, covering three separate client projects, certifications and shipping terms.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ answers are short paragraphs under each question.
findings.fix: In Site Factory, split the answer into short paragraphs (one per project, then one for certifications, testing and shipping), or shorten it and point to the cases section.
